You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

This looks like a "draw the mirrored/extended pattern" task? Let me think. Grid 20x10, mostly 5s with 8 lines. Full rows of 8 (rows 2,9,14,15,18) and full column of 8 (col 4). Other 8s scattered. Likely output: fill? Common task: lines of 8 indicate... Maybe the answer is the grid of full lines only — i.e., draw lines that separate cells into regions? Hmm.

Actually a common ARC task: 8s form partial lines (horizontal segments and vertical segments), output completes them into full lines across the grid. Here full rows and full column already exist; partial rows (like row 7: cols 2-4 and 7) and partial columns (col 2 rows 6-7...). Completing: each 8-marked line direction is signaled by existing full lines? Rows 0-1 have 8s in col 4 (that's the full column). Scattered 8s like row1 col0,col6 — isolated, ambiguous.

Alternative: output is the grid where you remove scattered 8s keeping only full lines? Too costly to guess. Better to request a demo.

I'll look at this pattern. The grid has full 8-rows, a full 8-column, and scattered 8s whose role is ambiguous — a demo is the safe move.

Demo: input has full lines of one color (6: full rows 2,14 and full columns 11,12), other color (8) is background. Output: full lines of 6 become 2; scattered 6s stay 6; 8s unchanged. So rule: replace the complete lines with 2 (or some third color = 2), keep partial marks.

Test input: background 5, marks 8. Full lines: rows 2,9,14,15,18 all 8, and column 4 all 8. Replace those full lines with 2? But what color—2? In demo, full 6-lines became 2. Scattered 8s stay. The demo shows the rule: lines of the mark color that span the entire grid (full rows/columns) become 2; scattered marks stay unchanged. Here full rows 2,9,14,15,18 and full column 4 become 2.
